description_text:
Ready to print Black Mask Batman DC 3D Printable Model (digital file). 
You can see my models after printing here: https://www.instagram.com/sonndersmith/
Final mask consists of 2 parts assembling together (front and back) by neodymium magnets (I recommend to use cylindrical magnets 8-10 mm in diameter and 4-6 mm in length). Both assembled parts have special conic recesses for drilling holes for magnets. 
You need at least 220 x 210 x 200 mm build volume to print the mask. Contact me if your printer is smaller and I’ll split the files up according to your parameters.
Average wall thickness of each big part has an optimal value for resin casting: 4-5 mm. 
I don’t mind if you’re going to sell masks made using my models, all I want from you is tagging me on Instagram in your relevant posts (@sonndersmith).
Listing contains:

  - set of printable files in OBJ format;

  - set of printable files of splitted helmet in OBJ format;

  - set of printable files in STL format;

  - low poly model of inner surface of the mask* in OBJ format. 

  - Before 3D printing you can check the mask size by making a low poly version of it out of paper using Pepakura. If the paper mask fits to your head well, you may print the file, if not, try to change its size at a certain percentage and when you find the proper value just use the same percentage for 3D printing. This approach will help you to save a lot of filament and time.

The mask model is scaled for an average 61 cm girth head, but the size could be changed if necessary. 
Contact me if you have any questions.

description_text:
Ready to print Master Chief Helmet 3D model (digital file). 
You can see my models after printing here: https://www.instagram.com/sonndersmith/
Final helmet consists of 2 main parts assembling together (base part and back part) by 2 pairs of neodimium magnets (I recommend using cylindrical magnets of 8-10 mm diameter and 5-8 mm length). Back part has special conic recesses for drilling holes for magnets. The helmet has many small high-detalized parts, which are sepatated from the main part and placed into individual files, so you can print the main piece by FDM printer and use photopolymer printing for small details (or just use better printing resolution for them). Both assembled parts have special conic recesses for drilling holes for magnets. 
Back detachable part has 3 pieces, two of them (chip holder and holder plate) can be made of transparent resin and then painted in some places, so you can make spectacular blue lighting for this part.
AI chip can be placed at any time into special slot of back part, it will stay there because of magnet attraction. There're special recesses for the magnets in the chip and in the holder.
You need at least 220 x 210 x 200 mm build volume to print the mask. Contact me if your printer is smaller and I’ll split the files up according to your parameters.
Average wall thickness of each big part has an optimal value for resin casting: 4-5 mm. 
I don’t mind if you’re going to sell masks made using my models, all I want from you is tagging me on Instagram in your relevant posts (@sonndersmith).
Listing contains:

  - printable file of solid helmet in OBJ format;

  - set of printable files of splitted helmet in OBJ format;

  - set of printable files of small details in OBJ format;

  - set of printable files in STL format;

  - low poly model of inner surface of the mask* in OBJ format. 

  - Before 3D printing you can check the mask size by making a low poly version of it out of paper using Pepakura. If the paper mask fits to your head well, you may print the file, if not, try to change its size at a certain percentage and when you find the proper value just use the same percentage for 3D printing. This approach will help you to save a lot of filament and time.

The mask model is scaled for an average 58 cm girth head, but the size could be changed if necessary. 
Contact me if you have any questions.

description_text:
All preview renders were rendered in Blender 2.8 using Cycles renderer with physically based Principled BSDF shader. Render setup utilizes 16384x8192 HDRI image lighting map (included).Textures are optimized for PBR rendering solutions (using Metalness or Specular workflows).Level 4 subdivision modifier is applied to geometry. Beauty renders uses albedo, roughness and vector displacement maps.
GEOMETRY
Geometry provided includes 3 low poly meshes. Each mesh is subdividable up to original sculpt level of 6 to accurately reveal all tiny details of displacement map.Model is designed to provide optimal detail/performance level you need. Not only high detail close-up renders are possible, but lower subdivision level/not subdivided mesh can also be used in game environments.

  - Geometry centered on the origin

  - Real world scale (units: centimeters)

  - Polygonal quads only

  - No poles with more than 5 edges

  - Displacement distance (useful in other software packages):  1.0 cm

  - UVs: linear

TEXTURES
Textures are photorealistic 4096x4096 (32 bit per channel EXR) images, created from real object capture data.Each of 3 meshes has its own uv map and textures.Each model UV's were created and inspected according to its specific surface characteristic. This enables to find the optimal balance of maximum texture space allocation, intuitive layout, easy further 2d texture editing possibilities and minimal texture distortion.Textures are designed to fit linear UVs (no internal smoothing, locked UV borders) to avoid UV smoothing errors. Geometry of evenly sized quads guarantees low linear UV texture distortion when subdivided.
Textures used in provided Blender scene:

  - Albedo

  - Roughness

  - Vector Displacement

  - Spherical 16384x8192 HDRI map texture

Additional textures provided in separate archive:

  - Normal (for subdivision level 0 geometry)

  - Specular

  - Glossiness

  - Displacement

  - Ground_rotten.obj (1536 polygons)

  - Albedo

  - Roughness

  - Vector Displacement

  - Normal (for subdivision level 0 geometry)

  - Specular

  - Glossiness

  - Displacement

No third-party plug-ins used.Scene created in Blender 2.8.

description_text:
Ready to print Goblin Slayer Helmet 3D model (digital file). 
You can see my models after printing here: https://www.instagram.com/sonndersmith/
Final mask consists of 2 parts assembling together (base part and front shield) by neodymium magnets (I recommend to use cylindrical magnets 8-10 mm in diameter and 4-6 mm in length). Both assembled parts have special conic recesses for drilling holes for magnets. 
You need at least 220 x 210 x 200 mm build volume to print the mask. Contact me if your printer is smaller and I’ll split the files up according to your parameters.
Average wall thickness of each big part has an optimal value for resin casting: 4-5 mm. 
I don’t mind if you’re going to sell masks made using my models, all I want from you is tagging me on Instagram in your relevant posts (@sonndersmith).
Listing contains:

  - printable file of solid helmet and front shield in OBJ and STL format;

  - the set of printable files of splitted helmet in OBJ and STL format;

  - low poly model of inner surface of the mask* in PDO and PDF format. 

  - Before 3D printing you can check the mask size by making a low poly version of it out of paper using Pepakura. If the paper mask fits to your head well, you may print the file, if not, try to change its size at a certain percentage and when you find the proper value just use the same percentage for 3D printing. This approach will help you to save a lot of filament and time.

The mask model is scaled for an average 57 cm girth head, but the size could be changed if necessary. 
Contact me if you have any questions

description_text:
Intro
I bet your second half did not think buying a 3D printer is a good idea, well, printing a gift of the vase may prove someone wrong! Highly detailed model of the vase is made in such a way as to allow for modular assembly. You can scale it as you want of course, but modularity allows for smaller size parts to be assembled later on.
Technical Info
Print parts one by one, then just glue them together. If you prefer to use one material, you can print the vase as one solid block (if it fits into your printer of course), this approach is faster and would save substantial amount of support material, which is otherwise needed when printing parts separately. The drawback of printing the vase as a solid block is that you loose aesthetical quality when nicely differentiating curved sections.
Further Note
If you need some extra information or something doesn't work, let me know and I will do my best to help. I hope you will like the end result! If you liked this item and you think others should try it, please rank it on this website or share the link on Facebook/Twitter, etc. Thanks!

description_text:
This is a photo-scanned, photo-realistic gravel driveway that has been edited to be tileable and low-poly.  There are only 176 polygons in the driveway itself.  These can be arrayed and bent along a curve.  I also have it set up for micro-displacement in case you need detail for a close-up shot.  The texture resolution is 500 pixels per foot, capturing almost every piece of gravel in the scene.  The size of the mesh is 22 feet by 8 feet, resulting in an 11,000 x 4,000 (44 megapixel) texture. 
The scene in Blender is set up with an example curve, the appropriate modifiers, and a material for micro-displacement.  For intermediate/advanced users, everything should be self-explanatory.  Note that the surface appears flat in the viewport. This is because the material setup only displaces the mesh while rendering.  If you're new to Blender, or something seems hard to understand, please don't hesitate to message.
The download includes: 

  - A 44 megapixel albedo texture.

  - A 44 megapixel displacement map to lower the wheel paths in the driveway (the Blender material has this set up).

  - Game-ready version (512p) of the original textures. 

  - The 22x8 plane object in a Blender file with all the necessary modifiers and material settings to make a seamless, curvy road. 

  - An example curve to show how the arrayed mesh can follow a pre-determined path (the curve must be applied before grass particles can grow on the entire mesh).

  - A basic group of example grass to demonstrate particle setups.

  - An OBJ version of the plane with UV unwrapping for use/modification in the 3D software of your choice.

  - Grave_Candles (5 meshes)

  - Cemetery_Fence with Gates (modular; 5 meshes)

  - All objects are polygonal, built in 3dsMax 2016 application.

  - Models are fully textured (PBR) 4096x4096/2048x2048/1024x1024 .pngs. Pack Includes texture set for Standard Roughness Setup.

  - Meshes, materials and textures share the same name.

  - Models are modular, so you can mix and match them as you like.

  - Polygons, Tris and Vertices-In total: 6 527  polys; 12 108 tris; 6 738 vertices.
WARNING: Pack includes just assets that are named in the asset list above. Additional objects seen in screenshots are not included and are used just for marketing purposes only.
